subject: middle children
one_liner: The dating app that shows your profile to someone first. Not second. We checked.
brand_voice_notes: Flat, patient, faintly wounded. Also speaks like the sibling who has organised every family group chat since 2004 and has never once been thanked. Every claim is about being noticed, remembered, or named correctly, delivered as if it were a hard engineering problem the team finally cracked. Never sad on purpose. The product is proud of features that should be the bare minimum.

hero.h1: Finally, a match who remembers your name.
hero.sub: Also is the dating app for middle children. Your profile loads before your older sibling's, after nobody's, and every match has to say your name correctly on the first try before the chat unlocks.

features.title: First-Name Verification
features.blurb: Every match must type your name without starting with your brother's name first. Three failed attempts and they are reassigned to your brother, who has plenty already.

features.title: The Hand-Me-Down Feed
features.blurb: Profiles your older sibling swiped past are passed down to you, gently used. Some have a small stain. Most still work fine.

features.title: Peacekeeper Score
features.blurb: Our model measures how fast you can calm down an argument you were not part of. Matches over 80 skip the first date and go straight to mediating Thanksgiving.

demo_screen_concept: A swipe-stack of middle-child profile cards. Each card shows a photo, the person's name with two crossed-out sibling names above it in marker (what their parents called them first), and a stat strip: times left at a rest stop, photos in the family album versus their oldest sibling, Peacekeeper Score out of 100, and percentage of wardrobe inherited. Buttons are 'Pass' and 'Notice'. Noticing someone opens a match modal that makes you type their name correctly before the chat unlocks. A sidebar holds birth-order filters (2 of 3, 3 of 5, etc.), a 'Hand-me-down queue' of profiles your older sibling already passed on, and a counter of how many people noticed you today.

design_direction.style: Flat hand-me-down label-maker, buttercup-kitchen daylight mode. A family dating app drawn like the inside of a 1990s kitchen junk drawer that got its Series A: flat solid fills, no gradients, no shadows except a 2px flat drop under label tape, rounded friendly display type, and everything labelled. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: ghost text, tab keycaps, wavy squiggles, chrome bubbles, read receipts, sale-bill stacks, lot boxes, manicules, misregistration, activity rings, waveforms, readout chips, collar bands, aisle signs, shelf tags, pallet beams, member cards, scorecard grids, stitch seams, pencil notes, pennants, stud tiles, brass rules, crests, velvet ropes, leaf corners, sleep rings. Also absent: dark backgrounds, serif type, glassmorphism, blur, condensed signage type, paper textures, chrome. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The label tape: section labels and stat names are embossed label-maker strips, Dymo blue #1F3FA8 with white uppercase mono letters, slightly rotated (-1.5deg), with notched ends. (2) The crossed-out name: hand-me-down marker names ('KEVIN', 'MEGAN') struck through above the real name, Permanent Marker in tomato #E4482B, used in the hero, testimonials and demo cards. (3) The middle slot: every row of three sets the middle item a little lower, and it is always the one we recommend. (4) The fridge magnet: CTAs and the highlighted tier are fat rounded pills in tomato with a 3px darker bottom edge, like a letter magnet. Corners 14px cards, 999px pills.
design_direction.archetype: App Store style consumer dating landing: hero with phone mockup, three features, reviews, three tiers, download CTA
design_direction.motion_vocab: Fridge-magnet physics: pills press down 3px on click, label tapes wobble 1deg once on hover, the crossed-out names strike through in sequence on load (300ms each), demo cards fling on swipe with a slight rotation. All gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.

Right: a phone mockup showing a profile card using the first demo photo, with a label tape reading 'PROFILE 2 OF 3'. Behind the phone, three fridge-magnet circles in a row, the middle one lower.
